svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The Maxwell\u2013Boltzmann distribution of particle energies in a gas."], [1, "At temperature T\u2081 most particles have moderate energy."], [3.5, "Only particles with energy \u2265 Ea can react: the shaded area."], [6, "At a higher temperature T\u2082 the curve flattens and shifts right; same area."], [9, "Many more particles now have energy \u2265 Ea: the rate increases."], [12, "A catalyst lowers Ea instead: more particles exceed it at the same temperature."]]
svg.title: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
svg.desc: Maxwell–Boltzmann distributions of particle kinetic energy at two temperatures, with the activation energy and the fraction of particles with enough energy to react, and the effect of a catalyst lowering the activation energy.
svg.text: Number of particles with each kinetic energy (fixed amount of gas).

g.data-info: Most particles have moderate energies; few have very high energy. The curve starts at the origin and never touches the energy axis at high energy.
The peak is lower and moves to higher energy; the area (total number of particles) stays the same.
The shaded area: much larger at T₂, so many more collisions are successful and the rate increases greatly.

g.text: E ≥ Ea at T₂: much larger area

g.data-info: Only particles with at least Ea can react when they collide.
Provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy: more particles have enough energy at the same temperature.

g.text: • far more particles with E ≥ Ea
